locator: §3.1, BHK-interpretation, 'knowing that a statement A is true means having a proof of it'
interpretation: Attribution reading of the section's first sentence, 'In intuitionism, knowing that a statement A is true means having a proof of it', recorded as it stands (STMT-KNOWING-TRUE-IS-HAVING-PROOF-INTUITIONISM). The norm of assertion the comparison uses, that what is asserted at a stage is proved there (STMT-ASSERTION-REQUIRES-PROOF-INTUITIONISM), takes asserting as claiming to know; that step is not the entry's and is the comparison's own open premise.
